name: Titanium Browser
statusNote: Renamed from Helium Browser for Android in July 2026 (release v150.0.7871.124) to avoid confusion with the unrelated desktop Helium browser
pitch: Vanadium-based Android Chromium that runs full MV2 desktop extensions.
summary: Open-source Chromium browser for Android built on GrapheneOS Vanadium patches, adding Manifest V2 and off-store extension install from the Chrome Web Store, Opera and Edge add-ons, or local CRX files.
bestFor: Android users who want full uBlock Origin and other MV2 extensions on a phone
Kiwi Browser refugees who want an open-source replacement
People who want a Vanadium-derived base without GrapheneOS
notFor: Users who need browser sync across devices
People wanting a polished, set-and-forget experience (experimental per coverage)
Anyone who expects GrapheneOS-level hardening on stock Android

pros.title: Full MV2 extensions
pros.detail: Installs extensions from Chrome Web Store, Opera Add-ons and Edge Add-ons, plus local CRX/ZIP and unpacked MV2 extensions.

pros.title: Full uBlock Origin
pros.detail: Community reports confirm the full uBO (not uBO Lite) installs from the Chrome Web Store.

pros.title: Open source, GPL-2.0
pros.detail: Builds are made on GitHub Actions and can be verified with the GitHub CLI.

pros.title: Fast Chromium updates
pros.detail: Release v156.0.8078.73 shipped 28 Oct 2026, tracking Chromium 156.

pros.title: Two install channels
pros.detail: Available on Google Play and GitHub Releases, and updates can move between them.

cons.title: No sync
cons.detail: No browser sync (bookmarks/tabs/passwords) was found in any source.

cons.title: Experimental
cons.detail: Coverage describes it as experimental with some stability trade-offs for the extra features.

cons.title: Hardening is weaker off GrapheneOS
cons.detail: The README itself says GrapheneOS with Vanadium offers stronger protection.

cons.title: Young single-developer project
cons.detail: Renamed in 2026 and maintained by one developer, with several forks appearing.

signatureFeatures: Titanium Extension companion (external download manager, dark mode, privacy options)

faq.q: Is Titanium Browser the same as Helium Browser for Android?
faq.a: Yes, it was renamed in July 2026 to avoid confusion with the unrelated desktop Helium browser; the Play package id is still io.github.jqssun.helium.
Yes, listed under developer jqssun (package io.github.jqssun.helium), and also on GitHub Releases.
Yes, the full MV2 uBlock Origin can be installed from the Chrome Web Store.

timeline.event: Released as Helium Browser for Android (jqssun), based on Vanadium

switching.note: No sync; install extensions from the Chrome Web Store or CRX. Bookmark import not confirmed.

sync.note: No sync found in any source (unverified)

passwordManager.note: No built-in vault confirmed; use Bitwarden etc. as extension or Android autofill (unverified)

mv2.note: Manifest V2 + secure off-store install patch; unpacked MV2 extensions loadable

privacy.defaults: Vanadium-derived hardening; Google services removed; no ad blocking by default

spec.telemetry: No telemetry documented; verify in app
spec.codecs: Chromium codecs, hardware decode via MediaCodec
spec.sandbox: Chromium sandbox + site isolation; hardening patches from Vanadium
spec.patchLag: Same-week Chromium stable updates (v156.0.8078.73 on 28 Oct 2026)

memory: Multi-process Chromium footprint typical for Android
cpu: CPU use comparable to Chrome for Android
battery: Chromium battery profile similar to Chrome on Android
resourceControls: No tab-sleep or energy-saver UI beyond Android defaults
lowEnd: Chromium wants a modern 64-bit phone with ample RAM
installSize: Full Chromium build; large download vs light browsers
privacyDefaults: Vanadium-derived, Google services stripped, but no ad blocking out of the box
blocking: Full MV2 uBlock Origin installable from Chrome Web Store
securityHardening: Vanadium patches, but README says GrapheneOS gives stronger protection
patchSpeed: v156.0.8078.73 released 28 Oct 2026, same stable as Vanadium
telemetry: No telemetry documented; de-Googled Vanadium base
lookCustom: Basic Chromium theming; dark mode via Titanium Extension
behaviourCustom: Few gestures or per-site controls beyond Chromium
advancedSettings: chrome://flags available, no deep policy tooling on Android
tabManagement: Chromium Android tab grid and groups; no vertical tabs
downloads: External download manager handoff via Titanium Extension
